questions.q: What does Grant say separates successful creatives from others?
a: They ship more ideas, not necessarily better ones
They keep work secret until it is perfect
They wait for one great burst of inspiration
They imitate whatever already sells well
questions.why: Lesson 1 says successful creatives do not have better ideas, they simply ship more of them.

questions.q: Why does the summary mention Picasso's output?
a: Volume, not just talent, produced his famous works
He painted only a handful of pieces
He destroyed nearly all his early work
He copied the style of his rivals
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes Picasso produced 1,800 paintings plus thousands of other works before becoming famous.

a: Unfinished tasks stay in the mind and can spark ideas
Finished work is remembered longer than unfinished work
Deadlines improve the quality of creative work
Group work produces more original ideas
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains the Zeigarnik effect: unfinished tasks linger in the mind until completed.

questions.q: How did Martin Luther King Jr.'s famous line emerge?
a: He improvised it after someone in the crowd urged him
It was written days in advance
His advisers inserted it into the script
He borrowed it from an earlier speech
questions.why: Lesson 2 recounts King abandoning his script after someone urged him to tell them about the dream.

questions.q: How can you make a novel idea feel less threatening?
a: Repeat it and tie it to familiar references
Present it once and never mention it again
Keep the details vague and abstract
Announce it only after it succeeds
questions.why: Lesson 3 recommends repetition and linking new ideas to familiar concepts like Shakespeare.
